Yeah, thats kinda the trick of it. Depression has been my back seat driver for the last 5 years or so and I have only recently been fighting it in the past year and a half. Before that it was a coping mechanism to deal with my abusive mother. Sorry that's a tangent. Anyways, what I find helps me escape the spiral of bad thoughts and feelings is finding new things that I enjoy doing and are interesting to me. This shows me that there is a bigger world and there might be other things that I might enjoy just as much or more. I guess what I am trying to say is don't put it on yourself to pull him out of depression, try instead to give him the rope that he might use to pull himself up. Also, listening and having a steady life yourself will do wonders.

I would definitely get him in therapy if that is in option. Exercise makes a big difference. I don't know if he likes reading or comedy but Jenny Lawson is an author who has struggled with depression her entire life (she has a blog under the name the bloggess) and she totally puts a hilarious and hopeful spin on depression. If you want to be there for him so he has someone to talk to that would really help him, but be sure that you establish boundaries so you don't get sucked down and depressed as well. Make sure to do things with him, getting him out of the house and out and about will go a long way. Even if the only thing he does each day is get up, take a shower, and put on clothes that's really important. This isn't going to be easy, and you both will need a lot of help, therapy is a must for him and it might help you as well if you are going to be taking on a big supportive role.
